title: PDL Week 11
coldOpen: I still have 4 weeks of power rankings to get through. Welcome to Week 11.

2: A team started Tre’ Harris and Kimani Vidal this week and got its first win of the season.
Harbaugh had to throw a flag to get Harris credit for his longest catch, but I’d go back to the third-and-four in the second quarter.
Herbert found Harris over the middle for 16 on a drive that ended in a touchdown.
Quentin Johnston wasn’t, and Herbert threw him one ball all night.
If I’m Joe, I don’t need Harris to take Ladd’s job.
I’m watching who gets that third-down throw when Ladd’s back and Herbert has all three of them to choose from.
Across the field, Jacoby Brissett threw 49 passes in his Baltimore debut.
Kyle McCord was the only one of the eight to score a point this week.
His first NFL start included a fumble the Colts ran in for six, and he still had the ball down two on Miami’s last drive.
Some of his better throws came late, after the Colts lost their top two corners.
Willis has to miss at least three more games, so Joe gets to see whether Miami will let McCord take those same shots before they’re down in the fourth and have to.
That’s more than he usually gets to learn about one of these guys before the starter comes back.
Miami’s only touchdown pass came from Malik Washington on a double pass.
I’d tell Joe to trade for him, but I want to see if he’ll do it without asking Sleeper to give him QB eligibility first.
3: Jeff was in the middle of scoring 215.48 when I decided to send him Stefon Diggs.
The first one is a fourth in 2028, so if Diggs beats you in the playoffs, I’d appreciate it if you could hold your complaint until I know who I’m taking.
The part of this week I found most offensive was that I could take away Jeff’s two quarterbacks and still have to deal with a team that scored 128.90.
McCaffrey caught two touchdowns that went for at least 66 yards each, and James Cook quietly got 157 on the ground.
This is also how Jeff got away with 3.70 from A.J. Brown and five from Travis Kelce.
There are weeks where a contender has to make up for that.
Jeff got to spend the second half of Sunday night watching Burrow throw with Cincinnati up three touchdowns.
I do think the Diggs trade makes sense for him.
Davante Adams is still on IR, Courtland Sutton was on bye, and I wouldn’t want to go into December figuring out which healthy guy to start every time Brown can’t go.
Diggs got ten targets on Thursday and caught the winner with 57 seconds left.
Jeff can use somebody who has that kind of job even on the weeks when the rest of his receivers are available.
He didn’t need to trade for a guy who could score 30.
He needed someone who can give him a reason to leave that third receiver spot alone for a few weeks.
What I’d like to see now is somebody make Wichita pay on the day the quarterbacks give him normal good games.
Max drew the week Mahomes threw five and Burrow threw four.
There’s a reasonable argument that anyone who gets both of them in the low twenties has an opening.
I’d just prefer to have made that argument before I gave Jeff another receiver.
4: Ja’Marr Chase had 231 receiving yards against Pittsburgh.
Unfortunately for Max, the quarterback responsible for all of them was starting for Jeff.
I’d have been asking the broadcast to cut away any time Cincinnati got inside the five.
Burrow threw three touchdowns from there, and none went to Chase.
The one he threw from farther out went to Meyers, who was on Max’s bench.
I don’t know how you’re supposed to watch your receiver catch 11 passes for 231 yards and come away wishing Cincinnati had spent a little more time throwing to him, but I think I’d have managed it.
The thing I’d spend time on if I were Max is running back.
C.J. Stroud gave him 25.44, and Cam Ward had 22.14 on the bench.
Start Ward over Bryce and the score goes from 98.54 to 112.58.
It looks better, and Jeff still has no reason to turn off the game.
Max started Woody Marks, Rachaad White and Jordan Mason and got 18.60 from the three of them.
He’s got another quarterback he can try.
I don’t see a move on the current bench that does the same thing for those running back spots.
Darren called Max the real chaos agent on the pod because his record was making life difficult for the teams trying to get into the playoffs on points.
Max is still 7-3. They’d all love for him to have to win on points instead.
He’s averaging 115, and the part that makes him awkward to rank is that he can trot out Chase and Stroud and make any one playoff matchup miserable.
I’d just like to see him buy somebody who lets him enjoy it when Chase puts up 231.
5: Jayden Daniels threw three touchdowns on Thursday.
I had Stefon Diggs, Jon had Antonio Williams and Ben Sinnott, and I was never happier to see Washington throw to a tight end than when I remembered which one Jon had started.
Williams and Sinnott both finished with 42 yards and a touchdown.
Thanks to the extra catches and our tight end premium, Jon got three more points from the guy I didn’t have to play against.
He had six receiving yards all season before Thursday and got some of his work while Chig was out.
I’m willing to give Jon credit for making the same decision I would’ve made, especially now that I’ve seen what it cost him.
The guy I wanted to go back and watch was Kaelon Black.
The 49ers were up one early in the third when he ran through two Cowboys for a 25-yard touchdown.
Later in the quarter he pitched it to Deebo Samuel on a reverse and Deebo went 70.
I understand why Sleeper won’t give Jon anything for that second one, but if I were him I’d at least make somebody tell me no.
McCaffrey had 223 yards and three touchdowns in that game.
He also had only two more carries than Black.
I figured Jon would eventually get a Sunday where Mendoza started and Jordyn Tyson got thrown to like somebody’s first-round pick.
That’s why he took them in the top four.
He spent the 4.03 on Black, and I thought we’d be checking McCaffrey’s injury report for a year before we had a reason to care who got the ball on the first drive after halftime.
6: Brian said on Disrespected that he was glad to be rid of his firsts because now he had no choice but to stay the course.
I’d been wondering what it would take to get Brian to stop changing his mind.
I appreciate that his solution was to make it more expensive.
He beat Greg with 145.68, and the player I kept going back to was Parker Washington.
He had 148 receiving yards before halftime against Tennessee.
The 50-yarder will get played back, but he also caught one at the sideline for 20 on a drive that ended in a field goal.
That’s a bigger deal for Hollywood than Bijan scoring a touchdown against Kansas City.
I already knew what Brian was buying there.
Washington giving him a third receiver he can start alongside Nico Collins and Tee Higgins is how you get to 145 on a day when Jordan Love scores 11.80.
Bhayshul Tuten is making some of those decisions easier too.
Brian got 26 carries out of him, and the Jaguars still threw him the ball.
The useful bit for Brian is that the last playoff spot has a points route, and 145 helps him there in a way a 105-point win wouldn’t.
He spent the podcast telling Brett to get him in and see what happens.
Looks like the playoff push is continuing as misfortune mounts for others.
7: Darren told me on the pod that scoring all those points would feel better if he weren’t in fifth place.
I don’t know how much better he felt on Sunday, but he did get 171 yards out of Jahmyr Gibbs before halftime in Germany.
I’d like him to try to remember that feeling the next time he tells me about his schedule.
The more impressive number is his 99 receiving yards.
Gibbs already had 153 on the ground.
Detroit could’ve had a perfectly good afternoon handing him the ball and leaving the rest to Goff, and instead Gibbs was a yard short of 100 as a receiver too.
It’s hard to think of a way to take his points out of a game.
On Thursday, Cam Skattebo did it a different way.
The Giants gave him the ball for both of their rushing touchdowns and got 44 yards out of him as a receiver.
I’m sure there were reasons to wonder what Darren was actually getting out of that second running back slot going into the week.
By Sunday afternoon I’d have happily taken either one.
I’ll hear the argument for Welch at three.
He has the better record and just put up 188 against Boulder.
Darren is averaging 159.8, more than 12 points better than Dallas, and Philadelphia got to 174 this week even with Brock Bowers going out and scoring 3.80.
One reason I’m willing to trust the average is that this team doesn’t always get there the same way.
This time it was the running backs.
George Kittle gave him something on a day Bowers couldn’t, and Stafford didn’t have to do anything in the fourth quarter to make the Rams’ game interesting.
Stafford is on bye next, so there’s a perfectly good chance Darren gets to remind me how much more convenient it would’ve been to move him to three on a different week.
8: I’ve spent some time complaining about Dak Prescott’s box scores.
He threw five touchdowns, Dallas kept coming back after going down 19 in the fourth, and Welch got a win out of it even though the actual Cowboys couldn’t.
If Dak ever wants to know what 43.42 looks like on the winning side, Welch can show him.
Emmett Johnson was another bright spot for the drip.
We already saw him catch passes downfield against Denver.
It was easy to look at that game and decide the Chiefs had found somebody they liked throwing to.
With Kenneth Walker out, they gave Johnson 22 carries.
He was already at 50 yards both rushing and receiving before halftime.
I don’t know how many guys we drafted in the second round who could get an NFL start on short notice and have everyone arguing about what the starter’s workload should look like when he comes back.
Welch got exactly 52 points from Johnson and Tony Pollard while Bucky Irving was on bye.
The last time I was talking about Pollard going off, he was on Welch’s bench, and I was trying to work out why I was starting Alvin Kamara.
This week, Welch needed him and got 19.90.
He also had a flex score under one and didn’t need Trey McBride to do anything remotely resembling his best work.
Fourth leaves Welch behind teams he can beat.
We know because he keeps doing it.
I’m still giving Darren credit for what he’s scored over ten weeks, but I don’t think Welch needs another big Dak game to make the argument anymore.
I’d be more interested in who the Chiefs hand the ball to the next time he only gets 20 out of him.
9: Brian brought up the idea of the Jets trading Breece Hall on Disrespected.
He figured Greg would be able to move Breece once he had a better job, and Brian would get to start Braelon Allen.
I respect going on a podcast to explain how the New York Jets could better serve both parties in a PDL matchup.
The Jets kept both of them.
Breece caught four balls for 67 yards, Braelon got eight carries, and Greg got to watch his quarterback, running back, and receiver all participate in a game where the Jets scored four field goals.
Geno went out, came back, and went out again.
I’d have more fun right now watching Blake Corum.
He’s had double-digit carries and a touchdown four games in a row.
On Sunday he got more carries than Kyren Williams and took the one-yard touchdown on the Rams’ first drive after halftime.
Brian got the first win between them after the Bijan trade.
Greg’s part of that deal was Emeka Egbuka, Jeremiah Love and Brian’s 2029 first.
Egbuka was on bye, Love was on IR, and the first-round pick remains unavailable for comment.
I put Hollywood ahead because I’d rather play London next Sunday.
If I were Greg, I’d be fine with Brian getting the better of the first Sunday in a trade whose whole point was to give me something to look forward to after this season.
10: I would’ve liked to watch the 49ers-Cowboys game with Mike.
When George Pickens kept scoring and making Dallas think it could come back, Mike got the points.
When Brock Purdy did something about it, Mike got those too.
It’s about as close as a person can get to rooting for the Cowboys without having to explain himself afterward.
There’s nothing useful to learn from the fact that it was enough to beat Joe by itself.
There is something useful in seeing Mike put up 184.60 on a week when Justin Jefferson didn’t score, Chris Olave caught three balls, and Ashton Jeanty had 18 rushing yards.
I used to look at Mike’s roster and start by wondering which of those guys was about to ruin my Sunday.
I’d have to get a lot further down the list before I got to an Isaac Likely game that starts on Thursday and leaves me mad for three days.
Likely took one 66 yards for a touchdown against Washington, but he had eight other catches.
That’s the part I’d be worried about if I drew Mike because he has never really had a strong TE.
A tight end can have a long touchdown and go back to getting three targets next week.
The Giants have been giving Likely enough work that, in our scoring, he doesn’t need the 66-yarder to put you in a hole.
He’s averaging 17.4 in Mike’s lineup view.
That’s more than most of us get from the receivers we’re actually proud to start.
I have Mike ahead of Max despite the records.
The gap between them is about 28 points a week, and I don’t need to use the Crocs matchup to make that case.

I’d still want another dependable running back if I were Mike. I’m considerably less excited about him finding one than I was when it looked like he needed Jefferson and Olave to be themselves every Sunday.
11: At the end of Disrespected, Brian and Brett were talking about who the contenders might want from the teams below them.
They got to Omarion Hampton and Brett said, “I want Hampton.”
I’m glad somebody finally asked the guy who owns him.
Darren beat Brett by 92, so I don’t know how much time Brett spent in the matchup tab on Monday.
I would’ve watched the Chargers drive anyway.
Harbaugh gave Hampton the ball on fourth-and-one, and when Herbert came up short at the goal line later in the drive, he gave it to Hampton on fourth down again.
He could’ve kicked and gone in ahead.
He wanted the touchdown and knew who he was asking for it.
If I’d spent the 1.02 on Hampton, that’s the drive I’d send somebody the next time they asked what I wanted for him.
Brett also told Brian he wasn’t giving away Trevor Lawrence or Jaxson Dart because he’s trying to build.
Lawrence got Jacksonville out of third-and-11 with his legs while Tennessee was still within seven, then threw his third touchdown of the day four plays later.
He’s already had five games with at least three touchdown passes this season.
We’ve done enough math on where Brett’s going to pick.
I’m more interested in what he does if the quarterback he was supposed to find somewhere in this rebuild is the one he already has.
Dart’s on IR, and when T-Mac has a quiet game, there isn’t another receiver Brett can count on to make up the difference.
That’s where I’d spend a pick if I were him.
We’ll probably still ask him about Hampton, because it costs us nothing to ask, and apparently we don’t listen to his answers the first time.
12: Welch beat Tanish, and I still have Tanish second.
I’m putting that in the first sentence so Welch doesn’t have to read all the way through Chuba Hubbard to get to the part he disagrees with.
Drake Maye went down on New England’s first possession in Munich.
The other quarterback on Tanish’s bench was Jameis Winston, who spent part of Thursday night asking the Commanders' defensive line who let the dogs out.
The Giants took a delay of game.
I don’t see a lineup decision Tanish missed here.
Chuba got 27 carries and another 80 yards as a receiver, and I like that he can get there without eating up all the work that makes Jonathan Taylor or Chase Brown useful in Tanish’s lineup.
Some of that running back depth we keep talking about is actually scoring at the same time now.
That matters on a week when Malik Nabers gives you 4.90 and one of the quarterbacks gives you three.
JSN was excellent again, which is becoming the least surprising thing I type about this team.
The Maye injury does change what I’d expect out of Boulder.
I’m keeping him here because Caleb is coming back from a bye and Jayden Daniels is already playing.
I don’t need to pretend the drop from Maye to whoever comes after those two is small.
We spent part of the last pod wondering if Tanish needed another receiver behind his top three.
He’s now had a much better demonstration of what it feels like when two names on a depth chart disappear at the same time.
I’d like his chances a lot more if he didn’t have to prove he could do it twice.
